[local] Product requirement: a representative single-process CLI and GUI workflow must run without containers or network infrastructure. Individual tools may declare network needs. This fixture states a requirement, not a passed test.
[isolation] Product requirement: a multitier host owns startup, routing, workspace/data isolation and cleanup. Two concurrent feature stacks must not collide or access each other's services or data. Docker networks are a candidate; plain process/systemd and Kubernetes may be consumer choices. The mechanism is undecided, not universal support.
[ownership] Ordinary authored Go owns workflow control flow. Gimbal supplies shared agent acceptance, scoped context/lifecycle semantics and source/event meaning. Consumers own compilation, orchestration, worker placement and storage policy. Temporal is one demonstrated target, not a mandatory dependency. A named web-app-plus-Postgres profile returning explicit app/database handles is a design candidate, not implemented universal capability.
[updates] Same-build Temporal replay has been demonstrated in a bounded consumer. That does not prove arbitrary workflow-version migration or restoration of live agent sessions. Retain a compatible generated build for its active runs, or drain them before replacing it. Target maintainers own deployment/update policy.
